paper_metadata.title: APPLICATION OF DEEP QUANTUM NEURAL NETWORKS TO FINANCE

summary: The paper studies a deep quantum neural network (DQNN) for two finance tasks: learning implied volatilities and learning option prices with Greeks. The reported simulations use 4 logical qubits for implied volatility (1 input, 1 output, 2 hidden) and 5 logical qubits for option pricing/Greeks (1 input, 1 output, 3 hidden), with 800 training iterations in the first experiment and 7 Black-Scholes training sets in the second. The paper reports good fit metrics in tables, but no classical-vs-quantum advantage or asymptotic speedup is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Deep quantum neural network (DQNN) trained to learn implied volatilities from strike prices using one input qubit, one output qubit, and one hidden layer; evaluated on market data with several choices of sigmoid parameters and hidden-layer size.

algorithm.variant: deep quantum neural network (DQNN) for supervised learning of implied volatility
algorithm.optimizer: classical parameter update via unitary update rule U -> e^{iK\epsilon}U
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initial states of U^l_j with seed 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Strike K and implied volatility sigma are mapped to single-qubit Bloch-sphere states using cos(P(.))|0> + sin(P(.))|1> with sigmoid-based preprocessing P(s,t,u).

problem_instance.description: Learning implied volatilities from strike prices in option market data.

dataset_specification.description: Strike-price / implied-volatility pairs; time to maturity fixed

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Market data converted to qubit states using sigmoid function P(F,K,beta) and P(sigma_K,K,gamma); implied volatility surface extension mentioned via sigma_K sqrt(tau)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of predicted outputs against training data for multiple beta/gamma settings; tables report per-strike differences and overall cost C

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Sigmoid-based mapping of strike and volatility to qubit amplitudes
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover implied volatility from output density matrix element X via inverse mapping

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup is reported; the paper presents numerical feasibility only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not assessable from the paper; only a small MATLAB simulation with 4 logical qubits is reported.

experiments.description: Deep quantum neural network (DQNN) trained to learn option prices and their Greeks (delta and gamma) from spot price and strike, using one input qubit, one output qubit, and one hidden layer; evaluated on Black-Scholes-generated training data with different differential-loss weights.

algorithm.variant: deep quantum neural network (DQNN) for option price, delta, and gamma learning
algorithm.optimizer: classical parameter update via unitary update rule U -> e^{iK_d\epsilon}U

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Spot price x, option value V, and their derivatives are mapped to single-qubit density matrices using sigmoid-based angle encoding P(x,K,beta) and P(V,K,gamma).
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize combined fidelity of price, first derivative, and second derivative: C_d = price fidelity + nu_d * delta fidelity + nu_g * gamma fidelity
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Derivative density matrices are rescaled with identity mixing to ensure valid quantum states (trace 1, positive eigenvalues)

problem_instance.description: Learning call option prices, delta, and gamma under the Black-Scholes model.

dataset_specification.description: Seven training sets of spot price x, call price V, delta dV/dx, and gamma d2V/dx2 with K=100, r=0.0, T=0.25, volatility=0.15

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Inputs and targets converted to qubit states via sigmoid function; derivative states normalized by adding identity/2 with scaling parameters mu_in and mu_out
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Tables compare predicted call price, delta, and gamma against training values for three settings of nu_d and nu_g

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Sigmoid-based mapping of spot price and option price to qubit states; derivative states rescaled to valid density matrices
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover predicted option price from output density matrix; recover delta and gamma from derivative-state observables

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is made; the paper reports only numerical comparison against training data.
